text: A payment just ended: how does the shop's server find out, without asking again and again?
prefix: A payment just ended: how does the shop's server find out, without asking again and again?

text: If the payment were saved first and the news published after it, a crash in between would lose the news forever, or announce a payment that never committed.
prefix: If the payment were saved first and the news published after it, a crash in between would lose the news forever, or announce a payment that never committed.

text: So the news goes into an outbox table, in the same transaction as the final status: they commit together, or not at all.
prefix: So the news goes into an outbox table, in the same transaction as the final status: they commit together, or not at all.

text: The payment raises the event itself, whenever it becomes paid, declined, failed, or sent to manual review.
prefix: The payment raises the event itself, whenever it becomes paid, declined, failed, or sent to manual review.

text: A listener writes it to the outbox while the payment is saved, inside that same transaction, with the trace it belongs to.
prefix: A listener writes it to the outbox while the payment is saved, inside that same transaction, with the trace it belongs to.

text: A relay runs every second, takes the oldest unpublished rows, and locks them with skip locked, so two instances never wait on each other or send the same row.
prefix: A relay runs every second, takes the oldest unpublished rows, and locks them with skip locked, so two instances never wait on each other or send the same row.

text: It publishes each one to Kafka, keyed by the payment, so one payment's events stay in order, and marks it published only after Kafka has it.
prefix: It publishes each one to Kafka, keyed by the payment, so one payment's events stay in order, and marks it published only after Kafka has it.

text: A crash in between sends it again, so every event carries its own id, and consumers drop repeats.
prefix: A crash in between sends it again, so every event carries its own id, and consumers drop repeats.

text: The merchant sets one webhook address per website: HTTPS, on the website's own domain.
prefix: The merchant sets one webhook address per website: HTTPS, on the website's own domain.

text: A Kafka listener posts the event there, signed the Standard Webhooks way with the merchant's key: an event id, a timestamp, and an HMAC signature that any Standard Webhooks library can check.
prefix: A Kafka listener posts the event there, signed the Standard Webhooks way with the merchant's key: an event id, a timestamp, and an HMAC signature that any Standard Webhooks library can check.

text: Any answer but a success is retried: one second, then two, then four, up to thirty, five times.
prefix: Any answer but a success is retried: one second, then two, then four, up to thirty, five times.

text: After that, the event is parked on a dead-letter topic for a person.
prefix: After that, the event is parked on a dead-letter topic for a person.

text: Every attempt is logged: where it went, and what the merchant answered.
prefix: Every attempt is logged: where it went, and what the merchant answered.

text: Postgres stays the truth, and Kafka only carries the news.
